title: 6.29.3 Lab: Jumps, and jumping again
description: moveKind learns a second answer, jump; doMove takes the jumped piece; and a piece that can jump again keeps the turn until it cannot.

steps.title: Run it
steps.instructions: This is your game from 6.28.3. Pieces step and the turn passes, but a piece next to an enemy cannot jump it.

steps.title: A jump is a second answer
steps.instructions: In `moveKind`, below `if (abs(dr) === 1) return 'step';`, add: `if (abs(dr) === 2) { const mid = grid[fr + dr / 2][fc + dc / 2]; if (mid !== '' && colorOf(mid) !== turn) return 'jump'; }`. Run and set up a jump (step a red piece next to a black one, with an empty square behind it). The jump moves, but the black piece stays: the next step takes it.
hints: `dr` is -2 or 2 here, so `dr / 2` is -1 or 1: one row toward the landing square.
If you brought your 6.28.3 work forward, your step test may look different; put the jump below it.

steps.title: Take the piece
steps.instructions: Make the first line of `doMove` `const kind = moveKind(fr, fc, tr, tc);`, before anything moves. After the two lines that move the letter, add `if (kind === 'jump') grid[(fr + tr) / 2][(fc + tc) / 2] = '';`. Run: a jump now takes the piece it jumps over.
hints: Ask `moveKind` before the piece moves. Afterwards the starting square is empty and the answer would be `''`.

steps.title: Jump again
steps.instructions: Add `let chain = false;` at the top and `chain = false;` in `newGame()`. Write `canJumpFrom(r, c)` from the reading, below `isLegal`. In `doMove`, after the jumped piece is taken: `if (kind === 'jump' && canJumpFrom(tr, tc)) { picked = { r: tr, c: tc }; chain = true; message = nameOf(turn) + ' jumps again!'; return; }`, then `chain = false;` on the line before the turn passes.
hints: `return` leaves `doMove` before the turn passes, so the same player goes again.

To see a double jump, add two lines in `makeBoard`, just before `return g;`: `g[4][1] = 'b';` puts a black piece in front of red, and `g[1][4] = '';` empties a square behind the black row. Red's piece on row 5, column 0 can now jump twice in one turn: over row 4, then over row 2. Take both lines out when you are done.

steps.title: Only that piece, only a jump
steps.instructions: Change `isLegal` to the reading's version: `const kind = moveKind(fr, fc, tr, tc);`, `if (kind === '') return false;`, `if (chain) return kind === 'jump' && fr === picked.r && fc === picked.c;`, `return true;`. In `clickAt`, the test that picks a piece up becomes `if (!chain && p !== '' && colorOf(p) === turn)`. Run: in the middle of a chain, clicking another piece or a step does nothing.

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch for "Lab: Jumps, and jumping again". The task: teach moveKind a second answer: 'jump' for two squares diagonally over a piece of the other colour (found halfway between the ends) onto an empty square; doMove asks moveKind before moving and empties the halfway square on a jump; after a jump, if the piece can jump again (canJumpFrom), the same player keeps the turn with that piece only and only a jump (chain), and otherwise the turn passes. Accept any names, helpers, ternaries, nested ifs, switch statements and semicolons; a line only in a comment or string does not count. Short, plain notes for a 14-year-old; never write corrected code.
